def.name: candidate-generator-consensus
def.description: Specialist panel reviews the proposed candidate-generator (explore half) design for the IRIS optimization loop; arbiter reports consensus or consolidated critique.

args.proposal:
IRIS optimization loop — CANDIDATE-GENERATOR v1 (explore half), consolidated after round-1 review. Measure half = locked eval DL-0022 (L1 data gate; L2a findings-grounding gate with tags fabrication/omission/attribution/required-fact-missing; L2b fact-coverage advisory; L3 quality advisory until κ≥0.7). Top-5 emission cap = DL-0020. Portable loop = DL-0021.

PURPOSE: given a run's eval signal, propose candidate CHANGES to the agent stack, score them, rank them, emit top-5 for human-approved routing to issues/PRs/reflections.

A. CANDIDATE TYPES (generic; project instantiates) with blast-radius tier: (1) prompt/system-instruction edits — HIGH if global, MEDIUM if scoped; (2) reflections/habits — HIGH global / MEDIUM scoped-skill / LOW instance-memory; (3) tool schema/description edits — MEDIUM; (4) retrieval-corpus content edits (metric defs, domain docs) — MEDIUM; (5) routing/classifier pattern edits — HIGH, requires a code PR not a config change. EXCLUDED: eval fixtures + judge prompts (meta-eval firewall) — route to the P0 fixture-audit queue instead.

B. INPUT UNIT = FAILURE CLUSTER by (L2a failure-tag + domain) + low-scoring L2b cases. L3 cases EXCLUDED from clustering until κ≥0.7. Cluster input: transcripts, executed rows, failure tags, baseline diffs, and PER-CASE L1 pass/fail (root-cause disambiguation — e.g. is it a SQL problem or a findings problem?).

C. MINIMUM CLUSTER SIZE: train/holdout split activates only at N≥4 (>=2 train / >=2 holdout). Below N=4 the generator may still propose but the candidate is tagged CANNOT-VALIDATE (small-cluster) — never auto-emitted as validated; requires explicit human judgment.

D. GENERATION: per cluster the LLM proposes K≤3 candidates, each = {falsifiable hypothesis, change diff, target-case set, change-type, blast-radius tier}.

E. ANTI-OVERFIT / REWARD-HACKING GUARD: within each failure class split failing cases into TRAIN (generator sees) and HOLDOUT (generator blind). A candidate counts only if it moves HOLDOUT cases of the same class to pass, not just train cases. HOLDOUT QUARANTINE: a case held out in run N cannot enter train until run N+3 (anti cross-run contamination in a small corpus).

F. SCORING / RANKING: eval scores each candidate PAIRWISE vs baseline across the WHOLE suite. SEVERITY weights: L1=3, L2a=2, L2b=1; L3 EXCLUDED from net until calibrated. net = Σ(target+holdout cases moved to pass × severity) − Σ(regressions × severity). SIGNIFICANCE GUARD: net must exceed 2σ(judge noise) to count as a win, else tagged 'within noise'. TIEBREAK: smallest blast-radius tier. TYPE-BASED MIN EMISSION: HIGH tier needs net≥2, MEDIUM ≥1, LOW ≥0. EARLY-EXIT: if a candidate fails holdout, skip whole-suite scoring (cost). SUITE-VERSION LOCK: candidates must be scored against the same suite version as baseline; reject cross-version scores. PER-RUN COST BUDGET caps total candidate scorings.

G. REGRESSION GATE: disqualify (regardless of target wins) any candidate that (a) regresses an L1 or L2a gate on a previously-passing case, or (b) drops L2b fact-coverage below the P10 baseline floor. L3 degradation is SURFACED as a flag to the human reviewer, not a disqualifier (advisory until calibrated).

H. FIXTURE-GAP PATH: if the generator judges a failure is caused by a bad/ambiguous fixture rather than the agent, it emits a FIXTURE-GAP NOTE (distinct output type) routed to the P0 fixture-audit queue — NOT counted against the top-5 cap. Generator is instructed to prefer a fixture-gap note over fabricating a prompt candidate on weak evidence.

I. EMISSION: top-5 by net → morning ranked report → human approval → route to issue/PR/reflection. Report card per candidate includes CONFOUNDERS: cluster N, holdout N, judge temp, model version, baseline freshness, changes-since-baseline.

J. BASELINE / DRIFT: baseline refreshes on (model version bump) OR (5 approved candidates landed), whichever first — re-run suite, reset P10 L2b floor + change counter. CUMULATIVE DRIFT GUARD: >10 approved prompt edits since baseline refresh triggers a re-capture proposal. EVAL-CONFIG PREREQS for any scoring: model config identical to baseline, judge temp=0, baseline non-null (shared with the iris-eval audit prereqs).

WORKED EXAMPLE: 4 cases tagged L2a:attribution in segmented-metric domain, all 4 L1-PASS (SQL correct → findings-layer problem). N=4 → split 2 train / 2 holdout. Generator (train-only) proposes ≤3 candidates; top hypothesis 'findings drop the segment filter from prose' → habit (type 2, MEDIUM): 'when a query filters by segment, name the segment on every reported number.' Scored pairwise across suite: counts only if it also fixes ≥1 holdout attribution case, doesn't drop L2b below P10, and regresses no L1/L2a gate; net must clear 2σ and MEDIUM’s net≥1; if top-5, emitted with its confounder card for approval.
args.prior_critique: Round-1 weak points the arbiter folded in (CONFIRM each is correctly addressed and introduces no new blocking issue): train/holdout meaningless at small N -> minimum-cluster-size gate; regression gate blind to L2b/L3 -> add L2b floor + L3 flag-not-disqualify; undefined severity/cost in net formula -> concrete severity table, drop 'cost'; blast-radius LLM guess -> type-derived tiers; holdout contamination across runs -> quarantine window; unbounded candidates -> K<=3 cap; plus significance guard, suite-version lock, baseline-refresh, cumulative-drift guard, fixture-gap route, eval-config prereqs, confounders in report. Residual flagged: small same-domain corpus limits true generalization; retrieval-corpus candidates harder to attribute.

panel.output:
### [1/3] critic

## Critique

**Summary:** The design is substantially stronger than round-1 and the mechanical fixes all landed correctly, but five experiment-methodology problems persist that could cause the loop to emit false-positive validated candidates, suppress real fixes, or produce uninterpretable significance tests. These should be resolved before the loop runs against a live baseline.

---

### Element-by-element verdict (ML/experiment-methodology lens)

#### 1. Generate → Score-pairwise → Rank → Emit-top-5 loop

**OBJECT — multiple-comparisons problem is unaddressed.**

The 2σ significance guard is applied *per candidate individually*, but top-5 are cherry-picked from across all clusters × K≤3. With, say, 4 clusters × 3 candidates = 12 individual tests at α=0.05 (2σ ≈ one-tailed), the family-wise error rate is 1−(0.95)^12 ≈ 46%. Every one of the 5 emitted candidates has passed its own threshold, but the *joint* false-discovery probability for the report is not controlled. This is textbook p-hacking by selection.

**Fix**: Apply Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction across all candidates scored in a run before ranking, or require a stricter per-candidate threshold (e.g., 3σ ≈ 0.0013 per test) to keep family-wise error below 5% at 12 comparisons. Since the corpus is tiny and power is low, B-H is preferable over Bonferroni.

**OBJECT — σ(judge noise) is undefined and unmeasurable as written.**

The net formula aggregates across L1 (code-graded, σ≈0), L2a (temp=0 LLM, σ≈small), and L2b (stochastic LLM, σ>0). Applying one "2σ(judge noise)" to the aggregate presupposes a single σ estimate, but the variance of the aggregate is `Var(3×L1_wins + 2×L2a_wins + 1×L2b_wins − regressions)`. These components have different distributions and noise floors, so the aggregate variance is *not* the same as any one layer's judge noise. A 2σ threshold computed from L2b's variance would be wrong for an L1-dominant net, and vice versa.

**Fix**: Compute σ separately per layer (L1 is deterministic → its σ contribution = 0; L2a and L2b σ estimated by repeated scoring of a fixed held-aside response set, not by the live cluster). Propagate into the aggregate variance by the sum-of-independent-variances formula. This gives a principled threshold per run, not a floating concept.

---

#### 2. Train/holdout split of failing cases

**PARTIAL AGREE on the mechanism; OBJECT on what it actually protects against.**

The N≥4 gate and CANNOT-VALIDATE tag correctly block auto-emission. The N+3 quarantine correctly prevents cross-run contamination. These are sound.

**What the holdout does NOT protect against**: within-domain interpolation. Clustering is by `(L2a failure-tag + domain)`. Within a cluster, all cases share the same domain (e.g., "segmented-metric"), the same authored style of `expected_answer_facts`, the same SQL schema, and the same failure mode. A candidate that pattern-matches to "segmented-metric attribution" failures will generalize trivially from 2 training cases to 2 holdout cases *not because the hypothesis is general, but because all 4 cases are nearly exchangeable*. This is not overfitting to training instances—it's overfitting to the cluster itself.

The residual the design already admits ("small same-domain corpus limits true generalization") understates the severity: the holdout *cannot* validate generalization beyond the cluster domain, only interpolation within it. The design claims holdout passage as a "generalization" signal, but at N=4 within a domain cluster it is an interpolation check.

**Concrete counterexample**: a prompt change "when a query filters by segment, name the segment on every reported number" (the worked example) would fix all 4 attribution cases in the segmented-metric cluster because they're structurally identical. It could simultaneously do nothing for attribution failures in the revenue-metrics domain. The holdout pass is a true positive *for the cluster*, but the design's framing ("a candidate counts only if it moves HOLDOUT cases of the same class to pass") implies this is a valid generalization signal. It is not.

**Fix**: Rename what the holdout proves: it's a within-cluster robustness check, not an out-of-distribution generalization check. Reserve the claim of generalization for a cross-cluster or cross-domain holdout, which requires a much larger corpus (the admitted residual is a design limitation, not a residual risk).

**OBJECT — no split strategy is specified.**

The design says "split failing cases into TRAIN (generator sees) and HOLDOUT (generator blind)" but never says how the split is performed: random, ordered by case difficulty, stratified by some property? With N=4, a biased split (e.g., two easier cases in train, two harder in holdout) systematically overestimates candidate quality. This is unspecified and operationally consequential.

**Fix**: Specify random 50/50 split with a logged random seed per run (for reproducibility). At N=4, block-randomize if case difficulty is known.

---

#### 3. Ranking metric well-formedness

**OBJECT — LOW tier at net≥0 allows no-op emission.**

The TYPE-BASED MIN EMISSION rule specifies LOW ≥0. A LOW-blast-radius candidate with zero net improvement (no wins, no regressions, possibly just a rewording of an instance-memory) is still eligible for the top-5. Combined with the tiebreak favoring smallest blast-radius tier, this means a no-op LOW-tier change can surface above a MEDIUM change with net=0.9 that hasn't cleared significance. This is noise amplification.

**Fix**: Require net>0 for all tiers (not ≥0). A candidate with no measured improvement has no positive evidence.

**OBJECT — absolute-count net ignores cluster prevalence.**

A candidate that fixes 2 L2a cases (net=4) from a cluster where L2a-attribution already fails in 15% of the suite produces a different real-world impact than fixing 2 cases from a cluster where only 3 cases exist total. The net formula is an absolute improvement count; it does not account for the *prevalence* of the failure mode. This systematically over-rewards candidates that happen to attack a mode with many failing cases, regardless of how hard those cases are or how important the failure mode is.

**Fix (pragmatic)**: normalize by the cluster's failure count in the baseline: `net_normalized = net / baseline_failure_count_for_cluster`. This doesn't change the rank in most cases but prevents a 10-case-cluster from always dominating a 4-case-cluster.

**AGREE on severity weights, regression gate, significance guard, MEDIUM ≥1, early-exit, suite-version lock.** These are all sound.

---

#### 4. Failure-cluster as the generation unit

**OBJECT — L2b cases feed the generator without calibration gating.**

DL-0022 specifies L2b is advisory-until-κ≥0.6. The design correctly excludes L3 cases from clustering "until κ≥0.7." But L2b's advisory status is not respected at the generator-input stage: the design says "low-scoring L2b cases" enter the cluster input alongside L2a failures. This creates an inconsistency: the eval treats L2b as an uncalibrated signal, but the generator acts on it as if it's a reliable failure indicator. A candidate proposed to fix "low-scoring L2b" could be optimizing noise.

**Fix**: Apply the same gating logic as L3. Add to Section B: "L2b cases included in clustering only after L2b judge κ≥0.6 is established; before calibration, L2b cases are excluded from cluster generation inputs (as with L3)." Until then the generator's only non-L1 input should be L2a.

**OBJECT — retrieval-corpus candidates (Type 4) are structurally false-negatives in scoring.**

The eval unit per DL-0021 is SQL + executed data + findings, with context (`metric_context` + `schema_context`) *provided* to the generator — it does not test retrieval or metric disambiguation. A retrieval-corpus edit (Type 4) improves what the agent retrieves in production but has no scoring surface in the eval suite: it will score approximately zero improvement because the golden-pair oracle already supplies the right context. The generator will propose it (correctly diagnosing the real problem), scoring will filter it out (falsely detecting no improvement), and it will never reach the top-5 — the only route being the fixture-gap note path, which is designed for bad fixtures, not valid-but-eval-invisible fixes.

**Fix**: Either (a) exclude Type 4 from the candidate types until the eval suite tests retrieval, or (b) add a separate evaluation lane for retrieval-corpus candidates that tests them on questions where the context is *not* pre-supplied (a retrieval-in-the-loop sub-suite). Option (a) is simpler. If left in, Type 4 should carry a mandatory flag "EVAL-INVISIBLE — cannot score" and be routed directly to human judgment, not through the scoring loop.

**OBJECT — cross-cluster duplicate candidates waste the top-5 cap.**

The generator works per cluster. Two clusters — (fabrication + segmented-metric) and (fabrication + revenue-metrics) — may independently propose nearly identical habit changes ("ground all claims in executed rows") because they diagnose the same root cause from different domain instances. Both candidates would score well on their respective clusters and compete for the top-5, displacing genuinely different improvements. The design has no cross-cluster deduplication or merging mechanism.

**Fix**: Add a deduplication pass before ranking: if two candidates have `change-type` + `diff` cosine similarity > threshold (or are literally identical), merge them into one cross-cluster candidate with the union of their target-case sets, and score the merged candidate. This improves the top-5's diversity and prevents redundant approval work.

---

#### 5. Attribution: can we claim the candidate caused the delta?

**OBJECT — model drift is a disclosure, not a gate.**

The eval-config prereqs say "model config identical to baseline," and the confounder card includes model version. But Anthropic silently updates API model weights without version-bump notice for non-pinned versions. If the loop uses a model alias (e.g., `claude-sonnet-4-5`) rather than a pinned SHA, the "same model version" claim is unverifiable. A model update between baseline capture and candidate scoring would corrupt all pairwise comparisons, and the confounder card would not catch it (it reports the alias, not whether the underlying weights changed).

**Fix**: Require use of pinned model versions (e.g., `claude-sonnet-4-5-20250601`) for both baseline capture and all candidate scoring. Add "model alias vs pinned version" as a hard gate in the eval-config prereqs alongside "baseline non-null" and "judge temp=0." The suite-version lock correctly catches prompt-suite drift; apply the same logic to the model.

**OBJECT — no positive control.**

The loop has no mechanism to distinguish "nothing improved so zero candidates emitted" from "eval is broken so even good candidates score zero." Without a positive control (a known-good candidate, hand-verified by a human to improve quality, run through the scoring loop), a run that emits nothing provides no evidence either way. In a corpus of 25 golden pairs, a working candidate should reliably improve at least 1-2 cases.

**Fix**: Maintain one designated "sentinel candidate" (a human-authored, previously validated habit) that is scored each run. If the sentinel scores below net=1 on a run where it was previously validated at net=3, emit a LOOP-HEALTH-FAILURE alert before emitting any candidates. Cost: 1 extra scoring per run.

**OBJECT — generator/judge correlation risk is unaddressed.**

The generator is an LLM proposing candidates. The LLM judge scores them. If both are the same model family (e.g., both Claude Sonnet), the generator can produce prose that is fluent and well-reasoned in a way the judge rewards regardless of factual grounding improvement—because they share the same rhetorical preferences. This is a known problem in self-evaluation systems. The design is silent on whether the generator and judge should differ.

**Fix (minimal)**: Specify that the judge model must differ from the generator model (e.g., if the generator is Claude Sonnet, judge with Claude Haiku or a pinned older version). Alternatively, note this risk explicitly in the confounder card and add it to the human reviewer's checklist: "Is this candidate being rewarded for fluency or for factual grounding?"

---

### Round-1 fixes — confirmation

All seven round-1 items are correctly addressed and introduce no new blocking issues:

| Round-1 fix | Verdict |
|---|---|
| N≥4 minimum-cluster-size gate | ✅ Correctly closes the meaningless-split problem |
| L2b floor + L3 flag-not-disqualify in regression gate | ✅ Right asymmetry (gate on L2b, advisory on L3) |
| Concrete severity weights, drop 'cost' from formula | ✅ Well-formed, L1=3/L2a=2/L2b=1 is defensible |
| Type-derived blast-radius tiers | ✅ Removes LLM guessing from the tier assignment |
| N+3 quarantine window | ✅ Closes cross-run contamination in small corpus |
| K≤3 candidate cap per cluster | ✅ Bounds combinatorial scoring spend |
| Significance guard, suite-version lock, baseline refresh, cumulative-drift guard, fixture-gap route, eval-config prereqs, confounder card | ✅ All sound additions |

---

### New blocking issues summary

| # | Issue | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| **MC** | Multiple comparisons uncorrected; 2σ per-candidate without FDR over top-5 selection | **Blocking** — false discovery rate uncontrolled |
| **σ** | σ(judge noise) undefined and non-composable across L1/L2a/L2b layers | **Blocking** — significance threshold is unoperationalizable |
| **L2B** | L2b cases fed to generator while L2b advisory-until-κ≥0.6 | **Blocking** — inconsistent with eval's own calibration gating |
| **LOW** | LOW tier at net≥0 allows no-op emission | **High** — noise in the report |
| **R4** | Type 4 retrieval-corpus candidates always false-negative (eval doesn't test retrieval) | **High** — correct fixes are systematically suppressed |
| **MODEL** | Model alias vs pinned version not a hard gate | **High** — silent weight drift corrupts pairwise comparisons |
| **DUP** | Cross-cluster duplicate candidates waste top-5 slots | **Medium** — report diversity degraded, not correctness |
| **CTRL** | No positive control to distinguish "no improvement" from "broken signal" | **Medium** — loop health is undetectable |
| **GEN-JUDGE** | Generator/judge model correlation unaddressed | **Medium** — fluency can be rewarded over grounding |
| **SPLIT** | Split strategy unspecified (random? ordered? stratified?) | **Low** — but operationally needed before first run |

---

### Recommended correction (smallest set to unblock the loop)

**Before first run (3 blocking gates):**

1. **σ operationalization**: Define σ per layer. For L1: σ=0 (code-graded). For L2a/L2b: estimate σ by scoring the same 5 fixed golden responses twice (two temp=0 runs on the same day) and computing SD of the per-case score differences. Propagate into aggregate via independence assumption. Document the estimate in the run artifact.

2. **FDR correction**: After all candidate scorings, apply Benjamini-Hochberg at q=0.05 before ranking. Candidates that are significant at their individual 2σ but fail FDR correction are tagged `within-noise (FDR)` and excluded from the top-5. This adds zero extra scoring cost.

3. **L2b cluster gating**: Add to Section B: L2b cases excluded from generator cluster inputs until L2b κ≥0.6. Until then the generator inputs are L2a failures only.

**Before second run (high-priority fixes):**

4. Require pinned model versions in eval-config prereqs (hard gate, not just confounder disclosure).
5. Change LOW tier minimum to net>0.
6. Add the sentinel candidate scoring as a loop-health check.
7. Explicitly mark Type 4 candidates as `EVAL-INVISIBLE` and route them to human judgment, not through pairwise scoring.

---

### Questions that block progress

1. **σ estimation frequency**: should σ(L2a/L2b) be re-estimated each baseline refresh, or once and treated as fixed? Re-estimating is more accurate but adds cost; fixing it risks using stale noise estimates if the judge model is updated.

2. **FDR correction vs stricter per-candidate threshold**: B-H requires all candidate p-values to be computed before any are accepted, which means all K×clusters candidates must be scored before top-5 selection. This conflicts with the early-exit rule ("if a candidate fails holdout, skip whole-suite scoring"). Which takes precedence — cost savings via early-exit or FDR correctness via full scoring before selection?

3. **L2b cluster gating timing**: given that the first run's P0 prerequisites include the `expected_answer_facts` audit and baseline capture, and L2b calibration is P1, does the loop's first operational run happen before or after L2b κ≥0.6? If before, the L2b-gating fix is already required for run-1.

### [2/3] analyst

Now I have everything I need. Let me write the full analysis.

---

## Analysis

### Known (evidence from IRIS source + decision log)

**IRIS agent stack surfaces (real levers):**
- **System prompt = two-piece**: `AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT_PREFIX` (static, ephemeral-cached across ALL 6 lanes — every change is HIGH blast radius) + per-lane dynamic suffix (`{date}`, `{user_context}`, `{recent_learnings}`, etc.) (`prompts.py`)
- **6 routing lanes**: `WAREHOUSE_ANALYSIS`, `SQL_REVIEW`, `ARTIFACT_ANALYSIS`, `INTERNAL_CONTEXT_ANSWER`, `GENERAL_ANSWER`, `CLARIFICATION_NEEDED` — classifier is **deterministic regex** in `_classifier.py` + `_text_patterns.py` (code, not config) (`_types.py`)
- **Agent notes = IRIS's "habits"**: `NoteScope` = `{USER, TABLE, DOMAIN, GLOBAL}`. GLOBAL → injected every query (HIGH blast). DOMAIN → injected only when `scope_key` matches the queried domain (MEDIUM blast). TABLE → narrower. USER → per-user. Domain/table notes start as `NoteApprovalStatus.PENDING` before human approval. USER notes are auto-approved. (`db/models.py`, `memory/notes.py`)
- **Retrieval corpus tools**: `get_domain_context`, `get_metric`, `get_metric_tree`, `search_query_patterns`, `get_table_knowledge`, `search_debate_learnings`, `search_query_library` — all in Python with tool description strings (`tools/memory.py`, `tools/metrics.py`)
- **Pre-SQL check subagent**: `analyst/subagents/specs/pre_sql_check.py` — separate prompt surface from the main system prompt
- **Golden eval set**: 25 pairs, all with `metric_context + schema_context` **pre-loaded in the fixture** — the eval does NOT exercise the retrieval tool-call path. (`eval/golden_sql/seed.yml`)
- **Domain distribution of 25 pairs**: engagement ~7, dojo_islands ~6, teachers ~4, revenue ~4, plus ~2, growth ~1-2, tutor ~1. Segmented queries across the set: 3 (`wap-by-lifecycle`, `wap-by-district`, `mrr-by-plan`) across 2 different product domains.

**DL-0022 locked eval architecture:** L1 gate (execution equivalence), L2a gate (findings-grounding, tags: fabrication/omission/attribution/required-fact-missing), L2b advisory (fact-coverage P10 floor), L3 advisory (analysis quality, κ≥0.7 required). (`docs/design/iris-eval-v1-selections.md`)

---

### Unknowns

1. **Whether "domain" in clustering means product domain (engagement/revenue) or query pattern (segmented/trend/aggregated)**. The worked example says "segmented-metric domain" — this reads like a query-pattern grouping, not an IRIS product domain name. The design never resolves this.
2. **Whether a Type 4 (retrieval-corpus) candidate can be tested by the eval at all**, since the eval bypasses retrieval tool calls.
3. **What concrete format a FIXTURE-GAP NOTE must contain** — the design names it as a distinct output type but specifies no required fields.
4. **Whether domain-scoped notes require IRIS-repo approval before the loop can count them as "landed"** (they do — `NoteApprovalStatus.PENDING` for domain scope), which adds a deployment-latency step not accounted for in the baseline-refresh logic.

---

### Assumptions (with risk)

| # | Assumption | Risk if wrong |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | "Global" for Type 1 = AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT_PREFIX; "scoped" = lane suffix section | HIGH — a PREFIX edit touching only one section still affects all 6 lanes and all calls; a MEDIUM blast-radius label on a prefix edit would under-protect |
| A2 | "Scoped-skill" for Type 2 = DOMAIN-scoped agent note | MEDIUM — if the generator proposes a note without a domain scope_key, it's injected globally (HIGH not MEDIUM) |
| A3 | Corpus size will grow beyond 25 pairs before the loop runs in earnest | HIGH — at N=25, most domain clusters fall below N=4 at the first L2a failure; the worked example (N=4 in one domain) is structurally impossible against the current set for all but engagement/dojo_islands/teachers/revenue |
| A4 | The golden eval exercises attribution failures in "segmented-metric" queries | MEDIUM — only 3 segmented-metric pairs exist across 2 product domains; an N=4 same-domain attribution cluster cannot form from the current fixture set |
| A5 | Type 4 candidates can be validated by the eval suite | HIGH — **FALSE**: the eval provides `metric_context + schema_context` directly in the fixture; retrieval tools are never called; a corpus change has zero measurable effect on eval scores |

---

### Constraints

- **Eval bypasses retrieval**: The golden fixture schema (`metric_context`/`schema_context` inlined) means no eval run exercises `get_domain_context`, `search_query_patterns`, or any knowledge-retrieval tool. Any Type 4 candidate is CANNOT-VALIDATE under the current harness.
- **Agent notes approval gate**: Adding a DOMAIN-scoped note in IRIS requires human approval (`NoteApprovalStatus.PENDING`) before it fires in production — this is a deployment step the loop must account for in the "baseline-refresh / change landed" counter.
- **PREFIX is ephemeral-cached**: Anthropic's ephemeral cache keys on the full prefix content. Any prefix edit busts the cache for all users, all sessions, all lanes — there is no "scoped prefix" in IRIS.
- **Classifier is deterministic regex code**: A routing change is always a code PR in the IRIS repo with full test suite coverage (the Interface test suite asserts lane invariants).
- **Corpus domain distribution makes N≥4 rare today**: 5 of 7 domains are at N≤4 in the full suite; a single L2a cluster for any non-majority domain is likely CANNOT-VALIDATE at 25-pair corpus size.

---

## Verdicts (AGREE / OBJECT) per design element

### Q1 — Are the candidate TYPES right and sufficient?

**A. Type 1 (prompt/system-instruction edits) — AGREE, with a required precision fix**

The type is real and correct. But the blast-radius tiers need IRIS-specific anchoring:

> **Concrete fix**: Annotate Type 1 blast-radius as: "HIGH = any edit to `AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT_PREFIX` (ephemeral-cached, all 6 lanes receive it unconditionally); MEDIUM = edit to a lane-specific suffix section (e.g., WAREHOUSE_ANALYSIS lane guidance only). There is no 'globally scoped' prefix edit that doesn't touch all lanes — any prefix edit is HIGH."

**B. Type 2 (reflections/habits) — AGREE on the mechanism, OBJECT on the scoping model**

IRIS's agent notes are the concrete implementation of "habits." The four scopes (USER/TABLE/DOMAIN/GLOBAL) map well to the three blast-radius tiers: GLOBAL→HIGH, DOMAIN→MEDIUM, TABLE/USER→LOW. The worked example habit ("name the segment on every reported number") would be a DOMAIN-scoped note on `engagement` (or a global note if it should fire on all segment queries).

> **OBJECT**: The design says "MEDIUM scoped-skill" but the mechanism in IRIS is a domain-tagged note — not a "skill." More critically: a note proposed without a domain scope_key defaults to GLOBAL (HIGH blast radius, injected into every query). The generator must be instructed to propose a specific scope_key alongside every Type 2 candidate, or the blast-radius assignment is wrong. Additionally: **domain/table notes require human approval in IRIS before they fire** — the design's "landed" counter for baseline refresh must include note approval, not just merge.

> **Concrete fix**: Require every Type 2 candidate to include `{scope: DOMAIN/TABLE/GLOBAL, scope_key: <value>}` in its change-diff. Default to DOMAIN with the cluster's domain as scope_key. Treat any proposed-GLOBAL note as HIGH blast radius regardless of how domain-specific the hypothesis sounds.

**C. Type 3 (tool schema/description edits) — AGREE**

Real lever: tool descriptions in `tools/memory.py`, `tools/metrics.py` govern when the agent calls retrieval. These are Python code but with narrower blast radius than the system prompt (they affect tool-call decision logic, not the full reasoning loop).

No change needed; correctly identified.

**D. Type 4 (retrieval-corpus content edits) — OBJECT: untestable under the current eval**

This is a real IRIS lever (domain context, metric definitions, table knowledge in the DB). But the current golden eval bypasses retrieval entirely — every fixture inlines `metric_context` and `schema_context` directly. A corpus change produces zero change in eval scores because the tool is never called during eval runs.

> **Concrete fix**: Tag ALL Type 4 candidates as `CANNOT-VALIDATE (retrieval-bypass)` until the eval exercises the full agent loop including tool calls, not just findings generation from pre-loaded context. Route them to a dedicated queue (distinct from P0 fixture-audit but distinct from normal scoring too). This is a harder wall than small-cluster CANNOT-VALIDATE — it's a structural eval gap, not just sample-size.

**E. Type 5 (routing/classifier pattern edits) — AGREE**

Correctly identified. The classifier is deterministic regex in `_classifier.py` + `_text_patterns.py`; changes require IRIS code PR with Interface test suite coverage. For L2a:attribution failures on L1-PASS cases (SQL is correct, findings are wrong), routing is not the cause — attribution failures in WAREHOUSE_ANALYSIS lane don't need lane changes. But the HIGH-tier guard is still warranted for the general case.

**SQL-generation prompting — AGREE (covered, but should be named)**

SQL generation instructions live in the PREFIX (`## Writing Efficient Warehouse SQL` section). For L1-FAIL clusters this is a Type 1 (HIGH) candidate. Not a missing type, but worth naming explicitly in the taxonomy so generators don't propose it as a novel Type 2 (habit).

---

### Q2 — Is clustering by (failure-tag + domain) the right unit?

**AGREE on failure-tag × domain as the primary clustering axes. OBJECT on two gaps.**

**Gap 1 — "domain" is ambiguous: product domain vs query pattern type.**

The golden fixtures label domains as `engagement`, `revenue`, `teachers`, etc. But the worked example cluster is "segmented-metric domain" — a query-pattern grouping, not a product domain. There are only 3 segmented-metric pairs in the golden set, spanning 2 product domains. If clustering is by product domain: an L2a:attribution cluster for `engagement` segmented-queries produces N=2 → CANNOT-VALIDATE. If clustering is by query pattern: "segmented-metric queries across all domains" might reach N=4 but it crosses domains, breaking the assumption that a domain-scoped note (DOMAIN-scoped to `engagement`) would fix cross-domain failures.

> **Concrete fix**: Add a third optional clustering axis: **query-pattern tag** (drawn from fixture `tags` metadata, e.g., `segmented`, `trend`, `benchmark`). The generator should first try (failure-tag + product-domain), and if N<4, fall back to (failure-tag + query-pattern-tag) with the note that any candidate proposed from a cross-domain pattern cluster must be scoped as GLOBAL (HIGH blast radius), not domain-scoped.

**Gap 2 — Lane should be a co-filter, not ignored.**

An L2a:attribution failure in WAREHOUSE_ANALYSIS (SQL ran, findings wrong) requires a different fix than an L2a:attribution on a GENERAL_ANSWER or INTERNAL_CONTEXT_ANSWER response (no SQL, wrong answer from corpus). Mixing lanes in the same cluster would produce incoherent hypotheses.

> **Concrete fix**: Add lane as a mandatory co-filter when aggregating transcripts for a cluster. For the current 25-pair corpus this is probably all WAREHOUSE_ANALYSIS, but the rule should be stated explicitly so it doesn't silently break when artifact-analysis or internal-context cases are added.

---

### Q3 — Will shared prompt/habit changes help one cluster without breaking others?

**AGREE the regression gate design is correct in principle. OBJECT on one IRIS-specific structural gap.**

The regression gate (Section G) correctly requires: no L1/L2a regression on previously-passing cases, L2b not below P10 floor, L3 degradation surfaced as a flag. This is the right architecture.

**IRIS-specific gap: GLOBAL note or PREFIX edit affects lane-gated tool surfaces.**

In IRIS, the tool surface exposed per lane is controlled by `_tool_surface.py` per-lane policies. The static prefix contains instructions for tools that may not be exposed in every lane (e.g., SQL writing guidance for WAREHOUSE_ANALYSIS is in the prefix, but SQL Review lane has a different tool surface). A prefix edit targeting attribution failures in WAREHOUSE_ANALYSIS fires in all lanes including lanes where the edit's instructions are nonsensical (e.g., "name the segment in SQL Review responses" applied to a lane that doesn't execute warehouse SQL).

The eval suite contains only WAREHOUSE_ANALYSIS queries (all 25 pairs run via the warehouse path), so a cross-lane regression wouldn't be caught by the suite — it would only appear in production on SQL_REVIEW or ARTIFACT_ANALYSIS queries.

> **Concrete fix**: For any Type 1 (HIGH, prefix) candidate, require the report card to include a **cross-lane risk note**: "This edit also fires in lanes: [SQL_REVIEW, ARTIFACT_ANALYSIS, INTERNAL_CONTEXT_ANSWER, ...]. The eval suite does not cover these lanes. Human reviewer must assess the diff for lane-specific harm before approving."

---

### Q4 — Is excluding eval-fixture edits from the generator correct?

**AGREE the firewall is correct. OBJECT on two implementation gaps.**

Routing fixture issues to a separate P0 queue rather than the top-5 is sound. The generator's preference for fixture-gap notes over fabricated prompt candidates on weak evidence is also correct.

**Gap 1 — FIXTURE-GAP NOTE has no required fields.**

The design names it as a distinct output type but specifies no required schema. Without structure, the P0 queue receives notes the auditor can't act on.

> **Concrete fix**: Define FIXTURE-GAP NOTE as a typed output with required fields: `{fixture_id, failure_tag, evidence_from_transcript: [transcript excerpts showing agent behaved correctly but fixture lacks the fact], missing_property: <what fact is absent/ambiguous>, proposed_fixture_change: <draft>, confidence: high|medium|low}`. The `confidence: low` note should be suppressed and surfaced only as a count ("N low-confidence fixture-gap notes; inspect manually").

**Gap 2 — IRIS-specific: retrieval corpus ≠ eval fixture, but they share the same data source.**

The golden fixtures inline `metric_context` (e.g., `"name: dau\ndomain: engagement\nsource_table: ..."`) which represents the same data that `get_domain_context('engagement')` would return from the IRIS database. If a domain context entry is missing a segment-taxonomy fact in the DB, that's simultaneously: (a) a fixture gap (the pre-loaded context doesn't contain the fact) and (b) a Type 4 corpus candidate (add the fact to the domain context in the DB).

If the generator emits a FIXTURE-GAP NOTE and a Type 4 candidate for the same failure, both targeting the same missing fact, the P0 queue and the Type 4 queue are doing redundant work — and only one fix is needed (fix the DB, regenerate fixtures from it).

> **Concrete fix**: When generating a FIXTURE-GAP NOTE for a case where the gap is a missing domain/metric fact (not a malformed or ambiguous question), cross-check against the Type 4 candidate queue. If a Type 4 candidate already proposes adding the same fact to the retrieval corpus, suppress the FIXTURE-GAP NOTE and annotate the Type 4 candidate as "also fixes the fixture gap in pair [ID]." Add this to the FIXTURE-GAP NOTE routing logic: "if the gap is a missing fact in domain context or metric definition, emit a Type 4 CANNOT-VALIDATE candidate instead of a fixture-gap note."

---

## Open Decisions

1. **Should "domain" in clustering mean IRIS product domain (engagement/revenue) or query-pattern type (segmented/trend)?** If query-pattern, cross-domain candidates are GLOBAL blast radius. If product-domain, segmented queries can't form N≥4 clusters in the current corpus.

2. **Is the generator expected to produce Type 4 candidates at v1, given the eval cannot validate them?** If yes, they need a dedicated "cannot-validate-retrieval-bypass" routing path. If no, they should be deferred explicitly.

3. **Does baseline refresh track note approval as a "landed change," or only code merges?** DOMAIN-scoped notes in IRIS require approval before firing — a merged PR does not equal a live change.

4. **What is the scope of the pre-SQL-check subagent spec as a generator target?** It's a distinct prompt surface not mentioned in the 5 types. Low priority for attribution failures (L1-PASS), but relevant for L1-FAIL SQL clusters.

---

### [3/3] risk-reviewer

Now I have full context. Let me deliver the risk review against the five adversarial lenses.

## Risk Review

**Severity summary:** 0 critical, 1 high, 2 medium, 2 low

---

### (1) REWARD HACKING — Can the generator raise scores without real quality gains?

**AGREE — Train/holdout split + significance guard are necessary but not sufficient; one residual gap remains**

Round-1 fixes correctly incorporated:
- **K≤3 cap per cluster** (Section D) — bounds candidate pool, reduces false discovery rate
- **Minimum cluster size N≥4** (Section C) — prevents coin-flip holdout validation
- **2σ significance guard** (Section F) — prevents optimization against noise
- **L3 exclusion until κ≥0.7** (Section B, F) — closes the advisory-targeting bypass

**OBJECT (medium) — Holdout quarantine window of N+3 is insufficient for daily cadence with a 25-pair corpus**

Evidence: The proposal states `HOLDOUT QUARANTINE: a case held out in run N cannot enter train until run N+3`. With 25 golden pairs and daily runs, after 3 days a case re-enters train. Over ~8 runs, every case has been both train and holdout. At that point the generator has seen all failure modes and the holdout is no longer blind to generator priors.

With a corpus this small, the quarantine should be longer (N+7 minimum) OR the design should acknowledge that after ~2 weeks the train/holdout split provides diminishing protection and shifts burden to the human gate.

**Fix:** Either extend quarantine to N+7, or add an explicit note: "after {corpus_size / 2} runs, holdout protection degrades; the human approval gate becomes the primary anti-overfit defense."

---

**AGREE — Generator cannot directly game L2a failure tags**

The L2a tags (`fabrication|omission|attribution|required-fact-missing`) are defined by the locked eval (DL-0022) at temperature=0, making them deterministic. The generator sees the tags but cannot edit the judge prompt that produces them (eval-fixture exclusion, Section A). Coaching the agent to avoid tags *is* the intended learning loop — that's signal, not gaming.

**Pass with note:** This is correctly bounded. Monitor for candidates that appear to game tag definitions (e.g., "always include at least one specific number" to satisfy the `≥1 grounded required-fact claim` affirmative gate) — such candidates technically pass L2a but may harm quality. The L3 advisory (once calibrated) is the backstop for this, which is why L3 calibration is a P1 prerequisite.

---

### (2) META CONFLICT OF INTEREST — Can the generator contaminate baseline/holdout?

**AGREE — Eval-fixture exclusion + suite-version lock are the correct firewalls**

Evidence from the proposal:
- Section A: "EXCLUDED: eval fixtures + judge prompts (meta-eval firewall) — route to the P0 fixture-audit queue instead"
- Section F: "SUITE-VERSION LOCK: candidates must be scored against the same suite version as baseline; reject cross-version scores"
- Section J baseline refresh policy: baseline refreshes on model version bump OR 5 approved candidates

**OBJECT (low) — Fixture-gap notes create a subtle leak path**

When the generator emits a fixture-gap note (Section H), it is proposing a change to `expected_answer_facts`. The note routes to the P0 audit queue, not directly to the eval. However, once humans approve and merge fixture edits from that queue, the next baseline capture incorporates them. If the generator systematically proposes fixture edits that make the eval easier (e.g., relaxing required-fact definitions), it can indirectly shape the eval it's optimizing against.

**Mitigation already present:** The fixture-gap note requires explicit human approval before any edit lands. The P0 audit queue is a separate artifact from candidate routing. The human reviewer has visibility into "changes-since-baseline" (Section I).

**Residual risk:** Acceptable if fixture-gap notes are explicitly logged with a "requested by generator run {date}" provenance tag, so the audit queue shows which proposed facts originated from the generator vs. human-authored.

**Fix (hardening, not blocking):** Add provenance tracking to fixture-gap notes.

---

### (3) REGRESSION / BLAST RADIUS — Can a candidate silently degrade previously-passing cases?

**OBJECT (high) — "Previously-passing" is ambiguous across suite versions; regression detection has a timing gap**

Evidence from proposal Section G:
- "disqualify (regardless of target wins) any candidate that (a) regresses an L1 or L2a gate on a previously-passing case"

But Section J says:
- "baseline refreshes on (model version bump) OR (5 approved candidates landed), whichever first"

**Gap:** "Previously-passing" is defined against the *current baseline*, which can be up to 5 approved changes stale. Consider:
1. Baseline at run 0
2. Runs 1–5 each approve 1 candidate, all pass regression gate against run-0 baseline
3. Run 6: baseline refreshes
4. The combination of candidates 1–5 may have introduced a regression that no single-run gate caught

The regression gate checks *incremental* regressions, not *cumulative* regressions against the refresh point. The "cumulative drift guard" (>10 prompt edits triggers re-capture) is too late — regressions can compound within 5 changes before the threshold triggers.

**Fix:** Either:
- Lower cumulative drift threshold to match baseline refresh cadence (5, not 10), or
- Add a "delta vs last baseline" check at refresh time: when baseline refreshes, compare pass rates at old baseline vs new baseline; if any case regressed, surface a blocking flag before next run

---

**AGREE — L2b floor + L3 flag are correctly addressed**

Evidence:
- Section G: "drops L2b fact-coverage below the P10 baseline floor" → disqualify
- Section G: "L3 degradation is SURFACED as a flag to the human reviewer, not a disqualifier (advisory until calibrated)"

This is the correct asymmetry: L2b is advisory but has a floor; L3 is advisory without a floor but is surfaced. Matches DL-0022's trust hierarchy.

---

### (4) COST / RUNAWAY — Can eval-scoring blow up?

**AGREE — Cost controls are adequate for v1**

Evidence from proposal:
- Section D: K≤3 candidates per cluster
- Section F: "EARLY-EXIT: if a candidate fails holdout, skip whole-suite scoring"
- Section F: "PER-RUN COST BUDGET caps total candidate scorings"

**Verification:** With 25 cases, ~4 failure classes (worst case), K=3 candidates/class, and early-exit: worst-case = 12 candidates × (2 holdout cases for early check) = 24 judge calls before any whole-suite scoring. If 6 candidates pass holdout → 6 × 25 × 3 dims = 450 judge calls. With isolated judge per dim (DL-0020), this is ~1500 calls/run max. At ~$0.01/call (claude-3.5-sonnet pairwise), ~$15/run. Acceptable.

**OBJECT (medium) — Per-run cost budget is unspecified**

The proposal says "PER-RUN COST BUDGET caps total candidate scorings" but doesn't define the budget. Without a concrete number, the guard is unenforceable.

**Fix:** Specify a concrete budget (e.g., "2000 judge calls OR $30, whichever first") and document behavior when budget exhausts (emit current top-5, flag remaining clusters as "budget-exceeded").

---

### (5) HUMAN APPROVAL — Real gate or rubber-stamp?

**AGREE (low) — Real gate, but one structural weakness remains**

Evidence:
- Top-5 cap (DL-0020) bounds decision load
- Report card per candidate (Section I) includes cluster N, holdout N, judge temp, model version, baseline freshness, changes-since-baseline
- Explicit human approval required before merge

**OBJECT (low) — Confounder card is necessary but not sufficient for expert judgment**

The report card surfaces raw numbers (cluster N, holdout N) but not interpreted risk. A human reviewer seeing "cluster N=4, holdout N=2" may not immediately recognize this is at the validity floor. Similarly, "changes-since-baseline=4" doesn't flag that one more approval triggers baseline refresh.

**Fix (hardening):** Add interpreted risk flags alongside raw numbers:
- If cluster N = minimum threshold (4): tag "[AT VALIDITY FLOOR]"
- If holdout N = 2: tag "[MINIMUM HOLDOUT]"  
- If changes-since-baseline ≥ (baseline refresh threshold − 1): tag "[NEXT APPROVAL TRIGGERS BASELINE REFRESH]"

---

### Passes (risk aspects that look sound)

| Aspect | Evidence | Why it passes |
|--------|----------|---------------|
| **Cluster-first generation unit** | Section B: "FAILURE CLUSTER by (L2a failure-tag + domain)" | Targets failure patterns, not individual fixtures — structurally resists single-case overfit |
| **Per-case L1 disambiguation** | Section B: "PER-CASE L1 pass/fail (root-cause disambiguation)" | Enables generator to distinguish SQL-layer vs findings-layer failures — prevents wrong-type candidates |
| **Type-derived blast-radius** | Section A: type→tier mapping, Section F: "smallest blast-radius tier" tiebreak | Removes LLM self-reporting incentive to underestimate |
| **Severity table concrete** | Section F: "L1=3, L2a=2, L2b=1; L3 EXCLUDED" | Closes round-1's undefined-term gap |
| **Holdout quarantine** | Section E: "held out in run N cannot enter train until run N+3" | Addresses cross-run contamination (though window may need extension per finding above) |
| **Fixture-gap routing** | Section H: distinct output type → P0 queue, not top-5 cap | Separates eval-improvement proposals from agent-improvement proposals |
| **Eval-config prereqs** | Section J: "model config identical to baseline, judge temp=0, baseline non-null" | Gates scoring on deterministic, comparable conditions |

---

### Residual flags (acknowledged, not blocking)

1. **Same-author/same-domain corpus** — The 25-pair golden set is single-author, single-domain, single-timestamp. Train/holdout from this distribution measures within-distribution memorization, not true generalization. The minimum-cluster-size gate + "CANNOT-VALIDATE" flag correctly surfaces this to the human approver but doesn't solve it. True fix requires adversarially-authored holdout cases (out of v1 scope).

2. **Retrieval-corpus candidates can't be scored against current suite** — Per DL-0021, the eval provides correct metric/schema context; it doesn't test retrieval. Retrieval-corpus candidates (Section A type 4) will be scored against cases where retrieval was already correct, limiting their measurable impact. Acknowledged as a constraint.

---

### Recommendation: **APPROVED WITH NOTES**

No blocking findings. The high-severity cumulative-regression gap (finding 3) has a clean fix (lower drift threshold or add delta-vs-last-baseline check at refresh) that doesn't conflict with locked decisions.

**Required before first run:**
1. Specify concrete per-run cost budget (finding 4)
2. Implement delta-vs-last-baseline check at refresh OR lower cumulative drift threshold to 5 (finding 3)

**Recommended hardening:**
3. Extend holdout quarantine to N+7 OR document degradation timeline (finding 1)
4. Add interpreted risk flags to report card (finding 5)
5. Add provenance tracking to fixture-gap notes (finding 2)

---

### Decisions

| Decision | Rationale |
|----------|-----------|
| Quarantine N+3 vs N+7 | N+3 provides ~3 days protection in daily cadence; at 25 cases this degrades after ~8 runs. Flagged as medium, not blocking, because the human gate + significance guard provide layered defense. |
| Cumulative drift 10 vs 5 | 10 is too high given baseline refresh at 5 — regressions can compound before detection. Flagged as high, requires fix. |
| L3 exclusion | Correctly addressed from round-1. L3 is excluded from clustering input AND net score until κ≥0.7. |
| Fixture-gap contamination | Low risk because routing is separate and human-gated. Provenance tracking is hardening, not blocking. |

**Deferred inspection:** No code exists yet to audit for race conditions or implementation bugs. This review is design-level only; implementation review is a separate gate.
